title: Finite-pattern factorization in a completed positive monoid algebra
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Let $G\cong\mathbf Z^r$ be a free abelian group of finite rank, and let $P\subseteq G$ be an additive submonoid generated by finitely many elements. Let $w:G	o\mathbf Z$ be a group homomorphism such that $w(p)>0$ for every $p\in P\setminus\{0\}$. Let $B=A^P$ be the ring of all coefficient families, with componentwise addition and convolution $(ab)_p=\sum_{u+v=p}a_ub_v$; these sums are finite under the stated hypotheses. Write $z^p$ for the family with coefficient $1$ at $p$ and $0$ elsewhere, and $C(a)=az^0$ for the constant embedding $A	o B$. Let $\mathfrak b\subseteq B$ be the ideal generated by $C(\mathfrak m)$ and the $z^p$ for $p
e0$. For $p
e0$, define $
u(p)$ to be the largest length of a decomposition of $p$ into nonzero elements of $P$ (a finite maximum under these hypotheses), and put $
u(0)=0$. For every integer $n\ge1$, every family $(a_p)_{p\in P}$ satisfying $a_p\in\mathfrak m^{\max(n-
u(p),0)}$ for all $p$ belongs to $\mathfrak b^n$. Here an ideal power $I^k$ is the ideal of finite sums of products of $k$ elements of $I$, with $I^0$ the whole ring.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, together with the explicit finite-pattern factorization supplied here; the source does not state this coefficient refinement verbatim.

proof.text:
Choose nonzero generators $g_1,\ldots,g_s$ of $P$, discarding zero generators; $s=0$ exactly when $P=\{0\}$. For $p
e0$, a decomposition $p=p_1+\cdots+p_l$ with $p_i
e0$ satisfies $l\le\sum_i w(p_i)=w(p)$ because each $w(p_i)$ is a positive integer. Such a decomposition exists with $l=1$, so the possible lengths form a nonempty finite subset of $\{1,\ldots,w(p)\}$ and have an attained maximum $
u(p)$. No nonempty sum of nonzero elements is $0$, since its weight is positive. For any $M\ge0$, an element of $P$ of weight at most $M$ is represented by a word of length at most $M$ in the $g_i$, since each generator has weight at least $1$. There are finitely many such words, including the empty word.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied coefficient refinement of the formal monoid algebra used there

proof.text: For fixed $p$, if $u+v=p$ with $u,v\in P$, then $0\le w(u),w(v)\le w(p)$. Step 1 gives finitely many possible $u,v$, so convolution is defined. Similarly, the triples $u+v+t=p$ form a finite set; expanding both bracketings of a triple product gives the same finite sum $\sum_{u+v+t=p}a_ub_vc_t$. This proves associativity, and commutativity, distributivity and the identity $z^0$ follow from the corresponding finite-sum formulas. In particular $z^uz^v=z^{u+v}$ and $C(a)z^p$ has coefficient $a$ at $p$ and zero elsewhere. Cancellation in $P\subseteq G$ gives the shift formula: the coefficient of $z^sc$ at $p$ is $c_q$ if $p=s+q$ for some $q\in P$, and is zero if there is no such $q$; that $q$ is unique.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied coefficient refinement of the formal monoid algebra used there

proof.text: Fix $n\ge1$ and put $S_n=\{p\in P:\nu(p)<n\}$. Any generator word representing $p$ is a decomposition into nonzero summands, so its length is at most $\nu(p)$; for $p=0$ use the empty word. Thus every $p\in S_n$ is the value of one of the finitely many generator words of length less than $n$, and $S_n$ is finite. This argument also covers $s=0$, when $S_n=\{0\}$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied coefficient refinement of the formal monoid algebra used there

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], choose generators $t_1,\ldots,t_h$ of the ideal $\mathfrak m$. For every $k\ge1$, expanding products of $k$ finite sums from $\mathfrak m=(t_1,\ldots,t_h)$ shows directly that every element of $\mathfrak m^k$ is a finite $A$-linear combination of products $t_{j_1}\cdots t_{j_k}$. Conversely each such product lies in $\mathfrak m^k$ by the definition of ideal multiplication. For $k=0$ use the empty product $1$. When $h=0$ and $k>0$, the ideal is zero and its elements have the empty-sum expression. Only distributivity and the definition of generated ideals are used.

source.place: Tag 00FM, section-Noetherian, first sentence; generated-ideal expansion is written explicitly

proof.text: For each $p\in S_n$, put $l=\nu(p)$ and choose a decomposition $p=p_1+\cdots+p_l$ attaining this length; when $p=0$, use the empty decomposition. Put $k=n-l>0$. The hypothesis and Step 4 express $a_p$ as a finite sum of terms $c\,t_{j_1}\cdots t_{j_k}$ with $c\in A$. Consequently $a_pz^p$ is the finite sum of $C(c)C(t_{j_1})\cdots C(t_{j_k})z^{p_1}\cdots z^{p_l}$. There are exactly $k+l=n$ displayed factors in $\mathfrak b$ after the scalar $C(c)$, so each term belongs to $\mathfrak b^n$. Summing over the finite set $S_n$ gives a family $a^{<}\in\mathfrak b^n$ equal to $a$ on $S_n$ and zero elsewhere.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied coefficient refinement of the formal monoid algebra used there

proof.text: Let $T=\{1,\ldots,s\}^n$, a finite set, and put $s_I=g_{i_1}+\cdots+g_{i_n}$ for $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_n)\in T$. If $\nu(p)\ge n$, choose a decomposition of $p$ into at least $n$ nonzero summands, write each of its first $n$ summands as a nonempty word in the $g_i$, and take one generator from each word. The remaining terms sum to $q\in P$, so $p=s_I+q$ for at least one $I\in T$. Fix an order on $T$ and assign $p$ to the first eligible $I$, meaning the first for which $p-s_I\in P$ in the ambient group $G$. This partitions $P\setminus S_n$ into subsets $E_I$. No $p$ is lost or counted twice. If $s=0$, there are no such $p$, so the partition and the sums below are empty.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied coefficient refinement of the formal monoid algebra used there

proof.text: For $I\in T$ define $c^I\in B$ by $c^I_q=a_{s_I+q}$ when $s_I+q\in E_I$, and $c^I_q=0$ otherwise. Every such family is an element of $B=A^P$; no convergence restriction is imposed. By the shift formula in Step 2, $z^{s_I}c^I$ equals $a$ on $E_I$ and is zero off $E_I$: cancellation ensures that each residual index contributes exactly once. Hence equality of coefficients gives $a-a^{<}=\sum_{I\in T}z^{s_I}c^I$. This is a finite sum, and $z^{s_I}=z^{g_{i_1}}\cdots z^{g_{i_n}}$ is a product of $n$ elements of $\mathfrak b$, so every summand belongs to $\mathfrak b^n$. Step 5 and closure under finite addition now give $a\in\mathfrak b^n$, as required.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied coefficient refinement of the formal monoid algebra used there

lean.statement: theorem finitePattern_factorization (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] (P : Type v) [AddCommMonoid P] [AddMonoid.FG P] (G : Type w) [AddCommGroup G] (ι : P →+ G) (hι : Function.Injective ι) (wgt : G →+ ℤ) (hpos : ∀ p : P, p ≠ 0 → 0 < wgt (ι p)) (hfree : ∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty (G ≃+ (Fin r → ℤ))) : ∃ ν : P → ℕ, ν 0 = 0 ∧ (∀ p : P, IsGreatest {k : ℕ | ∃ f : Fin k → P, (∀ i : Fin k, f i ≠ 0) ∧ (∑ i, f i) = p} (ν p)) ∧ (∀ p : P, Set.Finite {q : P × P | q.1 + q.2 = p}) ∧ ∃ ring : CommRing (P → A), (∀ p : P, (@Zero.zero (P → A) ring.toZero) p = 0) ∧ (∀ p : P, (@One.one (P → A) ring.toOne) p = if p = 0 then 1 else 0) ∧ (∀ (a c : P → A) (p : P), (@Add.add (P → A) ring.toAdd a c) p = a p + c p) ∧ (∀ (a c : P → A) (p : P), (@Mul.mul (P → A) ring.toMul a c) p = ∑ᶠ q : {q : P × P // q.1 + q.2 = p}, a q.1.1 * c q.1.2) ∧ ∀ (b : @Ideal (P → A) ring.toSemiring), b = @Ideal.span (P → A) ring.toSemiring ({x : P → A | ∃ t : A, t ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A ∧ x = fun p ↦ if p = 0 then t else 0} ∪ {x : P → A | ∃ q : P, q ≠ 0 ∧ x = fun p ↦ if p = q then 1 else 0}) → ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ a : P → A, (∀ p : P, a p ∈ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) ^ (n - ν p)) → a ∈ (@Ideal.instIdemCommSemiring (P → A) ring.toCommSemiring).toMonoid.npow n b
